sources.title: Drones sink ships near NATO countries in “unacceptable” attacks, EU says

items.title: For the First Time, Drones Sank Cargo Ships in NATO Members' Exclusive Economic Zones
items.body: Drones sank two cargo ships and damaged a third inside the exclusive economic zones of NATO member countries, killing at least two sailors. Ars Technica describes the sinkings as the first of their kind in those waters, which is what makes the episode more than another Black Sea shipping casualty. Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev called the attacks an “unacceptable attack in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone.”

sources.title: APOD: 2026 October 7 – Supernova Remnant Pa 30

discussion.body: Astronomers classify the explosion as a Type Iax supernova, an unusual variety, and think it was caused by the merger of two white dwarfs.
The dating is the real payoff. Because the guest star was recorded in 1181, a modern telescope image can be anchored to a specific year rather than to an estimate.

items.title: A “Guest Star” for 185 Days: The 1181 Supernova Behind Nebula Pa 30
items.body: Nebula Pa 30, observed with the Gemini North Telescope in Hawai’i, is likely the remnant of an old supernova explosion. Separate historical records by Chinese, Japanese and Arabic astronomers tell of a “guest star” that appeared in the sky for 185 days in the year 1181, and it is believed that the bright new point of light those astronomers saw came from the supernova that produced Pa 30. That pairing is the pleasure of the thing: a glowing nebula photographed this week is tied to a dated event reported in three different astronomical traditions eight centuries ago.

sources.title: Examining the DOJ's effort to prosecute non-citizens accused of voting

items.title: DOJ Presses Non-Citizen Voting Cases as Midterms Approach
items.body: Ahead of the midterm elections, the Department of Justice is leading a high-profile effort to catch and prosecute people it says illegally cast ballots, PBS NewsHour reports, sometimes holding televised press conferences to announce the cases. The same report states that there is no evidence supporting what it calls President Trump’s false claims of widespread voter fraud that skews election results. The prosecutions and the claims they are often packaged with are two different things.

sources.title: 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski spent investors' money on exotic cars, private jet flights: Crown

items.title: At the “Crypto King” Trial, Prosecutors Describe Cars, Jets and Credit Card Bills
items.body: The Crown gave an overview of its case against Aiden Pleterski, the self-described “Crypto King,” on the first day of his trial Tuesday. Prosecutors allege the 27-year-old spent investor money on himself — exotic cars, flights on private jets and credit card bills in the millions — instead of investing it in cryptocurrency and foreign exchange as he had told his investors.

sources.title: Arctic Sea Ice Shrinks to Its 2026 Minimum

items.title: Arctic Sea Ice Reached Its 2026 Minimum on September 12
items.body: Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum extent on September 12, 2026, tying several past years for the 10th-lowest minimum in the satellite record. NASA notes that satellite records show the ice now covers less of the Arctic Ocean at its annual maximum and minimum than it did a few decades ago, so the September low sits inside a range that has been shrinking at both ends.

sources.title: How did Quebec separatists win if most Quebecers oppose separation? | About That

discussion.body: Two questions were effectively on the ballot: whether to be done with the sitting government, and whether to leave Canada. Voters seem to have answered the first without endorsing the second.
True, but the party that now governs the province is still a separatist one. Sovereignty can be a separate issue on the campaign trail and still sit inside the government that won.

items.title: Quebec's Separatist Win, With Most Quebecers Against Secession
items.body: For the first time in over a decade, Quebec has elected a separatist party in its provincial elections, even though most Quebecers don't want to secede from Canada. CBC's Andrew Chang traces the result to the fall of the incumbent Coalition Avenir Québec, which led to the rise of the Parti Québécois.

sources.title: As some Afghans escape the Taliban, other refugees are forced to return

items.title: Afghans Are Still Fleeing — and Over a Million Are Going Back
items.body: PBS NewsHour reports that the Taliban's return in Afghanistan has brought economic collapse and deep uncertainty, especially for young people. Afghans are still trying to flee in search of safety. At the same time, more than a million who had escaped are now returning, many of them deported from neighboring countries.

sources.title: Manage Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Spaces directly from SageMaker Studio

discussion.body: The click-saving is the small half of this. The bigger claim is that one HyperPod cluster can serve interactive notebooks alongside training jobs and model deployment, with fractional GPU allocations, so teams aren't buying separate capacity for each kind of work.
That makes it a scheduling promise, not just a UI one. The open question is contention — what the cluster does when an interactive session and a long training run both want the same accelerators.

items.title: SageMaker HyperPod Spaces Move Into the Studio UI
items.body: AWS says it now lets teams create and manage Amazon SageMaker Spaces on SageMaker HyperPod EKS clusters directly from the SageMaker Studio UI. Data scientists and machine learning engineers can launch JupyterLab and Code Editor environments on HyperPod clusters without leaving the browser or dropping to command-line tools — by AWS's own framing, cutting the time from cluster access to productive development to a few clicks.

sources.title: Actress Eva Marie Saint, who won an Oscar for 'On the Waterfront,' dies at 102

items.title: Her First Film Role Won Her an Oscar
items.body:
NPR notes that On the Waterfront was Eva Marie Saint's first film job after years of theater and television — and it brought her an Academy Award. She played Edie, a Catholic schoolgirl whose longshoreman brother is murdered. From there she went on to star in Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest.

It is a strange pair of credits to have as a calling card: a social drama on the docks and a Hitchcock thriller, the earnest debut and the star turn. Both are the kind of films people rewatch for things other than their plots — casting, texture, the way a director uses a face.

sources.title: Where is Spain headed after the snap election announcement?

items.title: Sanchez Bets on an Early Election in Spain
items.body:
Spain is heading to an early election. Deutsche Welle reports that Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is taking a gamble by calling one, with the housing crisis, migration and the rise of the right-wing populist Vox party all likely to dominate the campaign.

A snap election is usually a bet that now is a better moment than the one coming. The campaign themes sketched out here suggest what the gamble is about.

sources.title: Sharing AI progress in mathematics

discussion.body: The notable thing isn't the model, it's the paper trail. Lean files and a public repository give skeptics something to dispute in detail instead of arguing about a demo.

Checking a proof can establish that the derivation holds; it doesn't establish that the result is what the problem was asking for. Those are two different readings, and only one of them is machine-checkable.

items.title: OpenAI Publishes Math Results and Lean Proofs From a Frontier Model
items.body:
OpenAI says it has published new results on open problems in mathematics produced by an internal frontier model, alongside Lean proof formalizations and research details on GitHub.

The Lean part is the interesting half. A formalized proof is a file a machine can check, which gives other mathematicians something to inspect line by line rather than a prose claim to accept or dismiss. What that artifact can't do by itself is establish that the statement it formalizes is the open problem everyone had in mind — and the publication is, at this stage, the company's own account of what its model produced.

sources.title: ‘Ash And Crayons’ Trailer: In Evgeny Afineevsky’s Film, Wounded Ukrainian Children Show Will To Survive And Thrive

items.title: A Ukrainian Children's Documentary Books World Children's Day for Its Release
items.body:
Deadline reports that Ash and Crayons, director Evgeny Afineevsky's documentary about Ukrainian children during Russia's war, will get a theatrical release on November 20 — World Children's Day — from Briarcliff Entertainment. The film focuses on seven children, and Deadline, which bills it as Oscar-contending, says it examines the horrors inflicted on Ukrainian children in the war and their will not only to survive but to thrive.

The date is not a neutral slot. Pairing a film about children with the international day dedicated to them is part of the release strategy, not a coincidence of the calendar.

sources.title: Ex-spy chief is arrested in Germany on suspicion of trading state secrets and treason

items.title: Germany Arrests a Former Head of Its Foreign Intelligence Service
items.body:
Germany's federal prosecutor's office says a former head of the country's foreign intelligence service was arrested on suspicion that he passed state secrets to a foreign intelligence service, NPR reports.

The accusation as reported is a suspicion, not a finding; the prosecutor's office has made an arrest, not proved a case. The job attached to the accused is what gives the detail its weight. Running a foreign intelligence service is the post whose purpose is keeping exactly this kind of material out of someone else's hands.

sources.title: Quebec’s anglophones approach PQ win with optimism, skepticism

items.title: Promises for Quebec's Anglophones, With a Referendum Still Possible
items.body:
Quebec's premier-designate has made several promises for the province's anglophones. Global News reports that the community is watching to see whether those promises are kept — with an independence referendum also possible.

That is a modest position to take, and a coherent one. Promises to a language minority are cheap at announcement time and only tested once a government's attention has some larger project to attend to, which a referendum campaign would be. Watching is what's left once the announcements have already been made.

sources.title: Josh Goldstine To Oversee Marketing And Distribution At All Skydance Film Labels Including Paramount And Warner Bros
Skydance Sets Leadership Across Games, Experiences, Consumer Products and HR

items.title: One Executive for Two Studios' Film Marketing
items.body:
Two organizational details from a very large merger. Deadline reports that Josh Goldstine, until now overseeing marketing at Paramount Pictures, is being tapped to head marketing and distribution for all of Skydance's film labels, Paramount and Warner Bros. included, after the merger closed Tuesday. Separately, Variety reports that Skydance says Paramount's and Warner Bros. Discovery's games and experiences divisions will be merged into one team that will oversee the combined projects.

The games line is the concrete one: two companies' worth of interactive projects now sit under a single group. The film line is about machinery rather than branding — one executive answering for how both labels' movies are sold and distributed. That is where a merger like this can start to be felt, not in a logo but in which films reach screens, and when.

sources.title: Chris Bourg named vice provost and Barbara K. Ostrom (1978) Director of the MIT Libraries

items.title: A Provost's Title for the Library Director
items.body:
Chris Bourg, who has directed the MIT Libraries since 2015, has been named vice provost and Barbara K. Ostrom (1978) Director of the Libraries, MIT Provost Anantha Chandrakasan announced. Chandrakasan's gloss on the new title is the interesting part: "vice provost," he said, "signals the enduring importance of the MIT Libraries in the digital age."

It is a small administrative change carrying a claim about priority — that a library belongs among an institution's senior concerns rather than off to one side as a service. Titles don't pay for anything. They only say what an institution thinks matters.

sources.title: Paramount completes $111B Warner merger, creating “Skydance” behemoth

items.title: A Court Said the Paramount-Warner Merger Would Likely Break Antitrust Law. Then It Closed.
items.body:
Paramount Skydance has completed its $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, Ars Technica reports. In July, US District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín in the Northern District of California ruled that the combination would likely reduce competition substantially and violate antitrust laws.

The price tag will get the headlines, but the ruling is the part worth keeping: a federal judge put a finding of likely anticompetition on the record, and the transaction is now complete.

sources.title: US death row inmate Christa Pike awake and speaking after failed execution, lawyers say

items.title: Christa Pike Is Believed to Be the Only Known Person to Survive a Lethal Injection
items.body:
Christa Pike, a US death row inmate, is believed to be the only known person to survive a lethal injection, the BBC reports. Experts and lawyers described her apparent recovery as unprecedented.

The hedge sits inside the claim itself — "believed to be the only known" — rather than in a statistic. It is not a distinction anyone would set out to hold.

sources.title: Eddie Redmayne’s Kore-eda Hirokazu Film Is Still Being Scripted, Director Says at Busan

items.title: Kore-eda Is Still Writing the Eddie Redmayne Film
items.body:
Eddie Redmayne's upcoming collaboration with Kore-eda Hirokazu is still at the screenplay stage, the Japanese director said at a Busan International Film Festival press conference for his manga adaptation "Look Back."

"Right now, I am writing the script," Kore-eda said about the Searchlight Pictures film. "I cannot share specific plot details at this stage." So there is no film yet, only a script in progress — which is what a status update sounds like before the marketing begins.

sources.title: Fact check: Misleading claims spark plague fears in Russia

items.title: A Plague Lab Worker's Death, and the Claims DW Flags as Misleading
items.body:
The death of a lab worker at a plague research institute in Russia has sparked claims about a lab accident, hundreds of infections and international spread. Deutsche Welle reports that some of those viral narratives are misleading.

One confirmed death and a story about hundreds of infections are different claims, even when they travel together — and the second is what turns a death at a laboratory into an outbreak rumor.
